annotation.title_clean: Commission Decision of 5 February 2014 on the safety requirements to be met by European standards for consumer laser products pursuant to Directive 2001/95/EC on general product safety (2014/59/EU)
annotation.title_en: Commission Decision of 5 February 2014 on the safety requirements to be met by European standards for consumer laser products pursuant to Directive 2001/95/EC on general product safety (2014/59/EU)
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.summary_en: EU Commission Decision 2014/59/EU sets safety requirements that European standards for consumer laser products must meet under the General Product Safety Directive, aiming to prevent eye and skin damage, with stricter rules for child-appealing products and warning labels where residual risk exists. It is unrelated to AI or robotics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Child-appealing consumer laser products must not cause eye or skin damage under any conditions of use
Other consumer laser products must not cause eye damage or unintended skin damage under foreseeable use
Conformity must be achieved by technical means
Residual-risk products must carry warning labels and user instructions
Decision enters into force the day after publication
